messages.subject: geom_hex for a percentage
parts:
Okay, let's imagine I have two data sets with lat, lons... df1 is let's say food inspections and df2 is restaurant licenses.

# may take a minute to dl data from chicago data portal...
df1 <- read.csv("http://data.cityofchicago.org/views/4ijn-s7e5/rows.csv",
               stringsAsFactors = F) 
names(df1) <- tolower(names(df1))

df2 <- read.csv("http://data.cityofchicago.org/views/r5kz-chrr/rows.csv",
               stringsAsFactors = F)
names(df2) <- tolower(names(df2))

I can do 

ggplot(df1) + geom_hex(aes(x=lon, y=lat))

and it will give me a nice hexbin graph of food inspections. But, this could be misleading, as more inspections will happen where there are more restaurants. What if I wanted to normalize this by the number of restaurant licenses?

Basically, for every bin, I want the count of df1 divided by the count of df2. 

How can I do this?

Thanks for your help.
